# S99 - Webhook resume, outbound webhooks and a Kafka consumer trigger (IN05)

26 October 2026. Implements roadmap item IN05 ([docs/25 section 6](../25-studio-and-integration-roadmap.md#6-in05---webhook-and-kafka-triggers)) on top of the EX10 callback model ([S98](S98-callback-tokens-and-triggers.md)), S47/S73 (signed inbound events, adapters, stub transport) and S16 (messages).

## Decisions

### (a) Signed inbound webhook that resumes a wait

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| A1 | The existing signed route `POST /workspaces/{ws}/inbound/{triggerId}` accepts an optional `X-Orqix-Callback-Token`. Signature, timestamp window, event id, 64 KiB and depth checks run first and unchanged. With a token the body is mapped by the trigger's `mapping` (field name -> JSON Pointer) into the **result** and handed to the EX10 resume service; no `inbound_event` is recorded, so the 1,000-pending cap is not consumed. |
| A2 | The token must belong to a request of the **trigger's own target workflow** in the same workspace; otherwise the answer is 404 exactly as for an unknown token. A trigger for workflow A can never resume workflow B, even with a valid token. |
| A3 | Idempotency key = `inbound:<triggerId>:<eventId>`, so a re-sent event replays the original result (`status: resumed, duplicate: true`). |
| A4 | Message content is data: neither body nor headers can choose the workspace, workflow, step or request; only the token (scoped to one wait) and the trigger (fixed workflow) do. |

### (b) Outbound webhooks

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| B1 | A workspace subscribes up to **10** HTTPS endpoints (`connection.manage`, fresh) to any of `request.started`, `task.opened`, `request.completed`, `request.needs-attention`, `callback.waiting`. They are derived from the run timeline (`RUN_STARTED`, `TASK_CREATED`, `RUN_COMPLETED`, `RUN_NEEDS_ATTENTION`) and the EX10 wait creation. |
| B2 | **Transactional outbox**: a delivery row is inserted in the same transaction as the timeline event, so an event is never lost and never sent for a rolled-back change. |
| B3 | **Payload: ids and states only** - `{id, type, occurredAt, workspaceId, request: {id, reference, workflowId, state}, step: {nodeId} or null}`. No input, output, task data, labels or names. A data-carrying option is not offered in this slice. |
| B4 | **Signing, domain-separated from inbound** (review fix): `X-Orqix-Signature: v1=hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "orqix-webhook-v1." + webhookId + "." + timestamp + "." + body))`, with `X-Orqix-Timestamp`, `X-Orqix-Webhook-Id` (the delivery id, stable across retries: receivers deduplicate on it) and `X-Orqix-Event`. The prefix and id make an outbound signature useless as an inbound `sha256=` signature (which covers `timestamp + "." + body`), so a webhook can never be used as a signing oracle for inbound triggers. The secret comes from a `secretRef` file, read at every attempt, that **must start with `webhook-`** and may not be used by any inbound trigger, adapter, connection binding or Kafka trigger (of any workspace); those in turn may not name a `webhook-` reference. |
| B5 | **Egress** (review fix): the URL must pass the existing `EgressPolicy` (https - plain http only for hosts the deployment lists in `orqix.egress.plain-http-hosts` for development -, exact `host:port` allow-list, public DNS unless approved private, no userinfo/query/fragment) when saved **and before every attempt**. At send time the host is resolved **once** by the policy and the connection is made **to exactly those vetted addresses** (a plain socket, or TLS layered on it with SNI, the `Host` header and certificate checks on the real host name), so a second DNS answer cannot redirect it (no rebinding). Redirects are never followed (a 3xx is an ordinary failed attempt). Connect timeout 5 s; TLS handshake, sending and the status line must finish within 15 s; the response body is never read or stored, only the status code. IPv4-mapped, NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`) and Teredo (`2001::/32`) addresses count as non-public. A refusal at send time dead-letters immediately (`egress_denied`). |
| B6 | **Retries**: any non-2xx or I/O error is retried with exponential backoff `initial x 2^(attempt-1)` (default 30 s, capped at 1 h) plus up to 10 % jitter, at most **8 attempts**, then `dead`. Missing secret is retried (`secret_unavailable`). |
| B7 | **Dead letters** are listed to operators (`run.operate`) with event type, request id, attempts, last status code and error code; **Replay** (fresh `run.operate`) resets one delivery to pending - refused while the subscription is paused, and 429 when the subscription already holds `max-pending` waiting deliveries. Audit `webhook.delivery-replayed`. Readers with only `connection.read` see a subscription URL as `scheme://host[:port]/…` (a path often carries a credential) and no secret reference. |
| B8 | **Multi-replica and isolation** (review fix): the dispatcher runs on its **own scheduler thread** (`webhookScheduler`), never on the shared one. It claims **one** due row at a time, right before sending, with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a 60 s lease (minimum 30 s, above the 20 s worst-case send), and writes the result back only while **that exact claim** still holds (same attempt number and lease); a pod whose lease expired can never overwrite a newer claim. A pass stops after 20 s; a subscription that failed once or used 5 s of a pass waits for the next pass, so one slow receiver cannot hold up other subscriptions or workspaces. Delivery is **at least once**. |
| B9 | **Caps**: 10,000 pending deliveries per subscription (beyond that the new delivery is recorded directly as dead with `pending_cap`, so it stays visible and replayable); at most 50 sends per pass per pod; **pausing a subscription dead-letters its waiting deliveries** (`subscription_paused`), so resuming never floods the receiver; delivered rows are deleted after 7 days, dead ones after 30. |

### (c) Kafka consumer trigger

| K1 | **Client library**: `org.apache.kafka:kafka-clients` (Apache License 2.0), version managed by the Spring Boot 4.0.8 BOM. Its runtime transitive dependencies are `zstd-jni` (BSD-2-Clause), `lz4-java` (Apache 2.0), `snappy-java` (Apache 2.0) and `slf4j-api` (MIT): all permissive. Not `spring-kafka`: we need explicit control of commits and fewer moving parts. Tests: `org.testcontainers:testcontainers-kafka` (MIT) with the `apache/kafka` image (Apache 2.0), test scope only. Resolved versions: kafka-clients 4.1.2, zstd-jni 1.5.6-10, `at.yawk.lz4:lz4-java` 1.10.1, snappy-java 1.1.10.7; recorded in [docs/07](../07-technology-decisions.md#open-source-boundaries); the CI CycloneDX SBOM lists them. |
| K2 | **Where brokers come from**: only from deployment configuration `orqix.kafka.clusters.<name>.bootstrap-servers` (+ `security-protocol`). A workspace trigger chooses a **cluster name** and a topic; it cannot type a host. Topics must also be listed in the cluster's `allowed-topics` (exact names, no patterns) - the allow-list. Credentials: a `secretRef` file holding JSON `username` and `password` (SASL PLAIN/SCRAM) - never accepted inline, never logged, never a `webhook-` reference. Two triggers of one cluster may not share a consumer group (unique index). |
| K3 | **Consumer groups and replicas**: each trigger has a fixed `consumerGroup` (default `orqix-<triggerKey>`). Every replica starts one consumer per enabled trigger in that group; Kafka assigns each partition to exactly one consumer of the group (cooperative-sticky assignor), so N replicas share the partitions and fail over on rebalance. |
| K4 | **Offsets**: `enable.auto.commit=false`. Each record is handled in its **own database transaction** that records it (`kafka_inbound_record`) and starts or resumes; offsets are committed (`commitSync`) only for records whose transaction committed - after every batch and in `onPartitionsRevoked`. A crash between commit of the row and commit of the offset re-delivers the record, which the dedupe key drops. **At-least-once delivery, exactly-once effect.** |
| K5 | **Duplicates**: dedupe key = the record key when present (1-200 printable characters), else `topic/partition/offset`; unique per trigger. A duplicate is skipped and counted. |
| K6 | **Ordering**: per partition in offset order. A transient failure (database unavailable, request busy, rate or quota limit) stops that partition at that record (`seek`) and retries with backoff 1 s..60 s; after **10** attempts the record is dead-lettered so a partition can never stall forever. |
| K7 | **Dead letters**: malformed JSON, oversize (> 64 KiB), too deep, unmapped/invalid fields, no active release, validation failures and exhausted retries become a `dead` record with an error code, partition, offset, key digest, size and SHA-256 - **never the payload**. The consumer always continues. Operators (`run.operate`) list them. They can be re-produced from the topic; replay from Orqix is not offered because the payload is not kept. |
| K8 | **Start** maps fields by JSON Pointer into the start input and calls the normal `RunService.start` **as the trigger's run-as person** (the person who created or last enabled it, who must hold `workflow.start` for the workflow); start permission, input validation, quotas and idempotency (`kafka:<trigger>:<dedupeKey>`) are the manual start's. **Resume** reads the correlation key by pointer and calls the normal `MessageService.send` with the configured message name as the run-as person (needs `message.send`); buffering, fan-out caps and payload checks are S16's. |
| K9 | **Caps**: at most 5 Kafka triggers per workspace; batch (`max.poll.records`) 1..100 (default 50); rate 1..200 records/s per trigger per replica (default 20); value at most 64 KiB, depth 10; mapping at most 20 fields. |
| K10 | **Visibility**: per trigger and replica a status row (assigned partitions, lag summed over assigned partitions, records handled, duplicates, dead letters, last poll, last error **code**) refreshed every poll; the API aggregates replicas. |
| K11 | **Modes per environment** (`orqix.kafka.mode`): `off` (**default**; triggers can be configured, nothing consumes), `stub` (no broker: a "Send test message" action pushes one JSON value through exactly the same handler - the demo mode) and `live` (real consumers). |
| K12 | **Security**: message content never changes routing - topic, workflow, message name and mapping are fixed by the trigger; content only fills mapped values and the correlation key. No message text in logs or audit: audit `kafka.trigger-created`, `kafka.trigger-updated`, `kafka.record-dead` (counts and codes). |

## What was built

- **(a)** `InboundService.receive` takes an optional `X-Orqix-Callback-Token`; after the unchanged signature, size, depth and source-filter checks the trigger mapping produces the result and the integration port `InboundCallbacks` (implemented by the runtime `CallbackService`) resumes the wait, refusing any request that does not run the trigger's workflow. `InboundAccepted` gains `status: resumed` and `waitId` (`eventId` is null then).
- **(b)** Migration `V171__outbound_webhooks.sql` (`webhook_subscription`, `webhook_delivery`); integration port `OutboundWebhooks` with `WebhookService` (outbox, subscriptions, secret name space, masking, pause, dead letters, replay limits) and `WebhookDispatcher` (own scheduler, per-row claim with fenced finish, time budgets, pinned connection, v1 signature, backoff, dead-letter, purge); `SecretNamespaces` keeps `webhook-` references out of connections, adapters, inbound and Kafka triggers; `EgressPolicy.checkAndResolve` returns the vetted addresses. Runtime `WebhookEvents` maps `RUN_STARTED`, `TASK_CREATED`, `RUN_COMPLETED`, `RUN_NEEDS_ATTENTION` inside the event's transaction, and `CallbackService` emits `callback.waiting`. API: `listWebhookSubscriptions`, `createWebhookSubscription`, `updateWebhookSubscription`, `listWebhookDeliveries`, `replayWebhookDelivery`. Settings → **Webhooks** (subscriptions, pause/resume, dead letters with Replay). Settings: `orqix.webhooks.initial-backoff` (30s), `max-backoff` (1h), `max-attempts` (8), `dispatch-delay` (5s), `batch` (50), `lease` (60s, at least 30s), `max-pending` (10000).
- **(c)** Dependency `kafka-clients`; migration `V172__kafka_triggers.sql` (`kafka_trigger`, `kafka_inbound_record`, `kafka_trigger_status`); `KafkaSettings` (`orqix.kafka.mode` off/stub/live, default **off**; `instance-id`; `clusters.<name>.bootstrap-servers`, `security-protocol`, `sasl-mechanism`, `allowed-topics`; `reconcile-delay`, default 10s); `KafkaTriggerService` (configuration with the run-as check, status aggregated over replicas that reported in the last two minutes, dead letters, stub test message); `KafkaRecordHandler` (one transaction per record: row plus start or message, dedupe, permanent versus transient classification, dead letters with digest and size only); `KafkaConsumerRunner` (one consumer per enabled trigger per replica, cooperative-sticky groups, manual commits after each batch and on revocation, pause/seek with backoff for transient failures, 10-attempt limit, rate pacing, lag and status rows); runtime port implementation `KafkaDispatcher` (normal `RunService.start` / `MessageService.send` as the run-as person). API: `listKafkaTriggers`, `createKafkaTrigger`, `updateKafkaTrigger`, `sendKafkaTestMessage`, `listKafkaDeadLetters`. Settings → **Kafka** (mode, configuration, status with lag/replicas/last error, pause/resume, stub test message, dead letters). `org.apache.kafka` logs at WARN; keys and values are never logged.
- Resume by Kafka goes through the message machinery (S16) by correlation key - the same delivery path EX10 callback tokens use; a Kafka record does not carry a callback token.

## Evidence

Covers S98 and S99, including the review fixes and IN05 (c). Runs in worktree `build-ex10-in05` on 26 October 2026 (JDK 21, Testcontainers PostgreSQL 18, Flowable, and a throw-away `apache/kafka:3.9.1` broker for the consumer tests). No existing container was touched.

- Full `backend/mvnw.cmd clean verify`: **BUILD SUCCESS** - compiler **613/613**; application **972** run, 968 pass, the same **4** intentional skips; coverage gate and packaging. (A first full run failed 4 `KafkaConsumerTest` cases only because another class's triggers had filled the 5-per-workspace cap in the shared test database; both Kafka test classes now start without triggers, and the rerun above is green.)
- EX10 / (a): `CallbackTokenApiTest` (7): issue once and hash-only storage, ETag 304, 400/422 without side effects, single resume through the message path with idempotent replay and 409 for a changed key or body, cross-request and cross-workspace 404, replaced/revoked tokens 404, run.operate boundaries, RUN_SUSPENDED until resumeRun, expiry poll/409 and one expiry audit, cancelled/requestEnded and answeredElsewhere, ordinary waits get no row, signed inbound resume limited to the trigger's workflow with duplicate replay; **revoke after resume refused (409) and the replay still answers 200**; **the token (and its hash) never appears in audit rows, captured log output or any problem/response body, including the inbound-resume path**. Compiler `MessageEventsTest` +2.
- (b): `OutboundWebhookApiTest` (11): permissions; egress refusal at save (allow-list, metadata address, userinfo, IPv6 literal, query); **webhook-only secret name space** (an inbound trigger's reference refused, a `webhook-` reference refused for inbound triggers, a `webhook-` reference already used elsewhere refused); **an outbound signature does not verify on the inbound endpoint even with the same secret value** (both `v1=` and re-labelled `sha256=` give 401); masked URL and no secretRef for readers; signed delivery with ids/states only and the real `Host`; 30 s first backoff, dead letter after 8 attempts, replay; **pause dead-letters the backlog, replay refused while paused and 429 at the pending cap**; **two dispatchers with a hanging receiver deliver every row exactly once**; **a late finish of an expired claim cannot overwrite the newer claim** (mutation check: with the fence removed this test fails with `pending` instead of `sending`); **a slow subscription uses only its budget so another subscription is served in the same pass**; dispatcher on its own scheduler; **connection pinned to the vetted address (a second lookup would point elsewhere, exactly one lookup per send)**; **a 302 to elsewhere is not followed**; **public-at-save then private-at-send refused before connecting**; IPv4-mapped, NAT64 and 6to4 answers refused; a stored URL with userinfo refused at send.
- (c): `KafkaTriggerApiTest` (3, stub mode): named clusters and allow-listed topics only, inline-credential refusal, run-as rights, duplicate consumer group/key 409, version conflict, audit keys; stub records start a request once, keyed repeat dropped, content that names another workflow or topic changes nothing, unmapped and invalid records dead-lettered without content (API, audit), resume by correlation key, missing key dead-lettered, unknown key buffered. `KafkaConsumerTest` (6, real broker): **a record starts a request once and a keyed repeat is dropped; malformed, unmapped and oversize records are dead-lettered while the good record after them is handled; a restarted consumer does not reprocess committed records; a resume trigger reaches the waiting request; two replicas in one consumer group each own exactly one partition, every partition's records were handled by one replica, and after one stops the other takes both partitions and finishes 60 records with 60 requests and no duplicate; a quota refusal is retried without storing anything and becomes a dead letter at the retry limit**. The second replica is a second consumer runtime with its own instance id in the same JVM, not a second process.
- `SecurityMatrixTest` covers every new operation (5 callback, 5 webhook, 5 Kafka) for foreign principals plus the machine issue route.
- Full frontend `vitest run`: **147 files, 1082 tests passed**. `tsc -b --noEmit` and `api:check` clean. `eslint .` reports **one pre-existing error** in `src/mocks/decisionCsv.ts` (irregular whitespace), a file this change does not touch. New or extended: `KafkaTriggersPanel.test.tsx` (2), `WebhooksPanel.test.tsx` (3), `CallbackWaitsPanel.test.tsx` (3; the token is not inside any live region, Copy announces success and failure), `MessageInspector.test.tsx` +1.
- `tools/contract-check/contract_check.py`: **PASS, 88 checks**.
- Not run: browser journeys and axe scans in a real browser (accessibility rests on labelled controls, status regions and component tests), Docker stack rollout, a two-process replica run, TLS/SASL against a real secured broker, and an https webhook receiver (TLS pinning is exercised only by code review; tests use the plain-http development host).

## Not included

- Callback: retention/purge of callback rows, per-token request rate limiting, a timeline entry for issue and revoke.
- Webhooks: payloads with request data, secret rotation UI, custom headers, mutual TLS, deleting subscriptions, an operator view of pending/delivered rows (API only).
- Kafka: replay of dead letters from Orqix (the value is not kept; re-produce it), Kafka record headers, schema registries/Avro, pattern topics, per-trigger SSL trust stores, a callback token carried by a record, automatic retention of `kafka_inbound_record`, deleting triggers.
